records.title: Air India: follow the sale cash, acquired debt and public cleanup separately
records.summary: Tata Sons→Talace acquired the public airline. The government actually received ₹2,700 cr; ₹15,300 cr debt stayed inside the acquired airlines. Excluded non-core assets valued ₹14,718 cr went to the public holding perimeter. The later Union Budget reports ₹62,365.40 cr actual FY22 equity to AIAHL—₹308.40 cr above the prior ₹62,057 cr estimate, driven by the past-dues component. These are different ledgers, not quantities to net into an unsupported “giveaway”.
records.dateBasis: Dates delimit documented events; status As Of is the latest supporting source date, not a claim of continuous current legal status.
records.period: Award 8-Oct 2021; closing 27-Jan 2022; actual FY2021–22 expenditure published 1-Feb 2023
records.response: Government says excessive losses/debt required an EV bidding model to improve competition, two bids exceeded reserve, and guarantees were to be released before closing. The record contains no adjudicated corruption finding.
alternativeExplanations: A loss-making airline may require balance-sheet cleanup to obtain competitive bids; historical creditor repayment is not automatically a benefit created for the buyer.
₹14,718 cr is asset valuation, not monetisation revenue, and cannot be subtracted as if realised.
Actual expenditure differs from the prior estimate; the difference is a normal reconciliation question until creditor-level evidence explains it.
records.falsifier: Obtain AIAHL audited ledger and creditor settlements, SPA schedules, independent valuation and realised asset-sale receipts; these could establish which liabilities/assets transferred and test any claimed net public cost.

records.title: Mangaluru: public airport→concession SPV→direct owners→parent finance
records.summary: The executed agreement connects AAI’s airport to CIN U63030GJ2019PLC110062. That CIN also identifies the later Mangaluru International Airport Limited. FY26 filings show 51% AEL and 49% AAHL direct ownership, with AAHL 100% AEL: a correction to the earlier 100%-AAHL shortcut. AAI reports ₹221.88 cr Mangaluru upfront capital reimbursement. The ₹710.88 cr concession-fee figure belongs to all six airports. Parent loan stocks finance the airport holding platform, without a site-level use-of-funds trace.
records.dateBasis: Dates delimit documented events; status As Of is the latest supporting source date, not a claim of continuous current legal status.
records.period: Concession signed 14-Feb 2020; receipts through Oct 2022; ownership/loan balances 31-Mar 2026
records.response: Government says AEL was highest bidder for all six under open competition. Article 27 bases original monthly fees on both embarking and disembarking traffic: ₹115 domestic, twice domestic for international, with revisions. Article 27.1.2 excludes concession fee from aeronautical cost pass-through.
alternativeExplanations: One corporate group can win multiple assets by bidding highest under common rules; six-of-six is a cohort result, not alone proof of rigging.
51% direct plus 49% through a wholly owned company gives effective group control, but does not mean AAHL directly owns 100%.
Loan stocks at the holding platform do not show which airport received the cash.
records.falsifier: Concession amendments, current SPV register, AAI airport-level monthly receipts and lender drawdown/use-of-funds schedules could falsify the ownership, fee or financing path; bid evaluation records would test competitive-treatment concerns.

records.title: HZL: government challenge, corporate rationale and procedural limits
records.summary: The 2021 Court allowed the residual public-stake sale and ordered investigation of the 2002 sale. DIPAM later disputed CBI premises, according to reporting. At the 29 April 2022 hearing, the government reportedly said an FIR had been registered. For the distinct 2023 related-party proposal, Vedanta claimed value creation, HZL said shareholder approval was required, the government dissented, and Reuters subsequently reported that the proposal had lapsed.
records.dateBasis: Dates delimit documented events; status As Of is the latest supporting source date, not a claim of continuous current legal status.
records.period: Court order in 2021; reported government challenge and FIR in 2022; separate proposal status in 2023
records.response: DIPAM said BNP adviser appointment and valuer selection had been mischaracterised. Vedanta said the 2023 deal would create a global zinc leader. HZL said no shareholder-meeting notice had been issued as of 20 February 2023. These are attributed responses, not accepted findings.
alternativeExplanations: Registration of an FIR is not a conviction; permission for share divestment does not exonerate every historical decision.
A related-party acquisition can have legitimate synergies; its pricing and minority-shareholder protection require specific valuation evidence.
records.falsifier: A primary FIR, closure report, charge-sheet or later Supreme Court order would update the historical inquiry. A 2023 approval and closing filing would establish whether the proposed acquisition ever became a completed transaction.

records.title: Hindustan Zinc: privatisation, retained state stake and a blocked cash proposal
records.summary: The government’s 26% sale to SOVL for about ₹445 crore ended HZL’s government-company status in 2002. A public open offer and call option later built a 64.92% holding. In 2023, Vedanta’s proposed US$2,981 million related-party asset sale would have used HZL cash while the government remained a minority shareholder and opposed the cash structure. The proposal reportedly lapsed, so it does not enter a payment ledger. Separately, the Supreme Court ordered investigation of the 2002 sale process while allowing the residual government-stake sale.
records.dateBasis: Dates delimit documented events; status As Of is the latest supporting source date, not a claim of continuous current legal status.
records.period: 2002–03 privatisation; 2021 court order; 2022 reported FIR; 2023 proposed related-party cash sale
records.response: The Court ordered a CBI case; it did not convict anyone or reverse the asset sale. DIPAM disputed factual premises in a reported recall application. Vedanta described the 2023 deal as creating shareholder value; HZL said shareholder approval was required. Reuters reported lapse from government sources and received no immediate response to its requests for comment.
alternativeExplanations: Residual government ownership can provide a minority-shareholder check after privatisation.
A commercial asset purchase may restructure a group without illicit purpose; valuation, minority approval and actual settlement determine its merits.
Historic SOVL ownership and Vedanta’s 2023 holding are separately sourced snapshots; corporate merger continuity is not proved by name association.
records.falsifier: Obtain the sale valuation and bid files, CBI case outcome, full 2023 valuation and minority-voting record, and closing or withdrawal filings. A completed cash settlement would change the proposal-only status; a valid valuation and approval record could weaken pricing concerns.

methodology: Four purposively selected developed corporate/energy/resource cases, not representative prevalence estimates.
Existing energy/capital/company/resource corpus mined first; exact legal identifiers rechecked where primary documents became available.
Accounting stage, financial perimeter and source date retained on every amount; no aggregate combines sale EV, government equity, fees, loans, income, receivables or proposed consideration.
Ownership snapshots are not backdated to the original award; direct and effective holdings distinguished.
Investigation, interim stay, rejected claim and final conviction are different statuses. Source publication is not evidence of current unresolved proceedings.
Public-source investigation only; no shared-address matching, inferred personal guilt or unnamed allegations upgraded into facts.
